thread:
sam: quick Q — we need UX guidance for when the system automatically enters a degrade/switchover mode. do we force a modal confirmation, or let it happen and surface an audit card?
elaine: prefer no blocking modal. auto-actions should be non-modal unless human action is required. show a transient banner + audit card in the route history. :eyes:
jun: question: what signals should trigger auto-degrade? we have: sustained 5xx > 2% for 5m, p95 latency > 800ms for 3m, and quota exhaustion fallback. are we ok with these defaults?
maya: those defaults seem reasonable but need a hard cap for oscillation. maybe add a cooldown window (default 10m) and a backoff multiplier.
sam: yes — cooldown and a reverse-eval window. also want an explicit "reason" that shows up in the audit log (so SREs can filter).
elaine: UI suggestion: show degrade mode as a pill with two flavors: `soft-degrade` and `hard-degrade`. soft-degrade = route to cheaper model / reduce batch sizes / shed noncritical features. hard-degrade = return a degraded placeholder or strict error.
jun: implementation-wise soft-degrade is safer to auto-apply. hard-degrade should be opt-in for auto-actions. default policy: auto -> soft, manual -> hard allowed.
sam: +1. also should we require a short human note for any auto-action that lasts > 15m? like an audit comment after the fact?
maya: I'd rather avoid interrupting teams. auto audit entry with auto-generated summary and a CTA to add a note. if no note added within 24h, ping owners.
elaine: for the console, we can have a compact timeline card: [timestamp] Entered soft-degrade (p95 920ms) — reason: latency-p95 > 800ms for 3m. expand -> shows request sample, policy id, decision trace.
sam: decision trace retention question — how long should we store traces for auto-degrades? 30d default?
jun: 30d seems fine. approved for default retention, with enterprise-configurable retention policies. log should contain: request_id, model_version, policy_id, selected_route, fallback_variant, and metrics snapshot.
elaine: UX nit: add a filter in the policy list for "auto-applied" vs "manual" with quick toggles to mute notifications for known maintenance windows.
sam: also add a "snooze auto-degrades" control per-route (timeboxed) so an on-call can pause auto-actions for 10/30/60 minutes. it should still record events but not switch routes.
maya: agree. make snooze require an owner and optional comment. audit entry should reflect snooze window and owner.
jun: ops-bot: propose a concise policy DSL for the console so we can render UI fields and validate server-side. sample: 
```yaml
policy_id: latency-auto-1
mode: auto
preferred_action: soft-degrade
triggers:
  - signal: latency.p95
    threshold_ms: 800
    window_minutes: 3
  - signal: http.5xx_rate
    threshold_percent: 2.0
    window_minutes: 5
cooldown_minutes: 10
max_consecutive_auto: 3
retain_decision_traces_days: 30
notifications:
  slack: true
  email: false
```
elaine: great — console can expose the top-level fields and an "advanced" YAML editor for power users. validation errors should be inline.
sam: question for product: do we show the exact threshold values to end-users or only recommended presets?
elaine: show presets (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with a "custom" option that reveals thresholds. avoid exposing raw kernel names; keep it human-friendly.
jun: telemetry: every auto-degrade event should emit a breadcrumb: `{policy_id, trigger, metric_value, model_version, route_from, route_to, request_sample_id}` so downstream analytics can surface regression roots.
maya: +1. also add a sampled payload for privacy (default sample rate 1%) and pii-scrubbing.
sam: security/compliance asks: audit entries must be tamper-evident. ops-bot: can we append signed audit entries?
ops-bot: yes — when an auto-action executes, I will append an audit row: `auto-action|policy=latency-auto-1|cid=2531122334|sig=sha256:...` and surface a link to the archived trace.
jun: final thing — rollback UX. if the auto-degrade caused worse outcomes, user should be able to "revert" to prior route and optionally annotate why. revert should create a follow-up audit entry and increment a counter for policy reliability metrics.
elaine: UI mock: left rail policy list -> center timeline -> right rail quick actions (snooze, revert, annotate). small footprint so it doesn't block primary ops flows.
sam: thanks all. next steps: elaíne + design to sketch the timeline card and pill states; jun + infra to wire the telemetry breadcrumb schema; maya to own snooze API; ops-bot to generate example audit entries. we'll sync in the weekly eng-platform standup. :thumbsup:
